title: x402: An open standard for internet-native payments (whitepaper)

No rolling chargeback windows [...] Instant, finalized transactions—No chargebacks, no fraud risks, no intermediaries. [...] Payments settle instantly onchain, eliminating chargebacks and disputes. [table: x402 (on Base) Chargeback Risk: No - not reversible]

title: Scheme: auth-capture (network-agnostic spec, v1.1)
quote: Where exact moves a fixed amount once and offers no way to give it back, auth-capture is for payments whose final amount is not known when the client authorizes, or which may later need to be undone. [...] reclaim is the client's unilateral escape hatch and is never relayed through the facilitator. [...] Later operations are named on the settle payload [...] No new facilitator endpoint is involved. [...] Held funds remain recoverable once the capture deadline passes, so a resource server that abandons a payment cannot strand it forever. [v1.1 2026-08-18; v1.0 2026-05-13]

title: Scheme: auth-capture on EVM (binding spec, v1.1)
quote: What the server gives up is enforcement: nothing onchain requires an authorizer signature [...] so the facilitator's own verification is the only gate. [...] within those bounds it is trust, not proof. [...] The pair (capturableAmount, refundableAmount) cannot recur once either balance has moved [...] No nonce is kept anywhere: the payment's own state is the replay key. [...] For operatorType: delegated this check runs only at the facilitator [...] making the guarantee best-effort. [...] A facilitator MUST reject type: refund for a delegated operator unless it has an explicit out-of-band funding agreement with the receiver [...] one that delegates both is captive to this facilitator until its refundDeadline [...] The Solidity in the appendix illustrates a future addition rather than audited or deployed code

title: Commerce Payments Protocol: Security Analysis
quote: Operators cannot steal funds from the protocol. Malicious or inactive operators can censor payments by failing to move a payment through its lifecycle or by prematurely voiding payments. [...] in the worst case, an operator could siphon the maximum configurable fee rate to an address of their choosing. [...] escrowed funds for a given operator are stored in a dedicated TokenStore contract deployed at an address deterministically derived from the specific operator [...] Some tokens, such as USDC, implement denylists [...] cannot later be captured due to a blocked recipient or feeReceiver.

title: Engineering the Commerce Payments Protocol Powering Shopify
quote: [Jun 12, 2025] Coinbase and Shopify are launching the Commerce Payments Protocol [...] Traditional payments handle this with a two-step authorize and capture process: first locking buyer funds (authorize), then disbursing them to the merchant (capture). [...] we introduce a new role called an operator to facilitate movement of funds between the transacting parties.

title: Introducing the commerce payments protocol
quote: most onchain payments today work well for peer-to-peer transfers, they fall short of handling the complexity of commercial purchases [...] Captures can be made in multiple partial increments to support merchants that may fulfill goods in multiple deliveries. [...] Coinbase provides an operator service, but the protocol is open for anyone to build their own.

Coinbase then captures and settles it server-side, with no hosted page, wallet pop-up, or human required. [...] The funds are held in escrow until Coinbase captures them. [...] Treat the checkout reaching COMPLETED as the source of truth for settlement. [...] Refunds are asynchronous
